claims.text: The initial TiVNbTa alloy is a single-phase dendritic BCC material without secondary precipitates.
Adding a small amount of carbon during processing will enable TiC precipitates to form in the TiVNbTa alloy.
The carbon addition will produce a uniform dispersion of nanoscale TiC precipitates.
The proposed TiC precipitates will remain thermally stable under elevated-temperature service.
TiC precipitates will impede dislocation motion in the BCC matrix at high temperature.
TiC precipitates will stabilize grain boundaries at high temperature.
Precipitation strengthening will mitigate high-temperature softening in TiVNbTa.
The baseline TiVNbTa alloy has a yield strength of approximately 330 MPa at 1273 K.
The baseline TiVNbTa alloy has a compressive strength of approximately 423 MPa at 1273 K.
The carbon-modified alloy will have higher yield strength at 1273 K than the approximately 330 MPa baseline.
The carbon-modified alloy may attain a yield strength in the mid-400s to 500 MPa range at 1273 K.
The strengthened alloy will retain sufficient ductility for use as a structural intermediate layer.
The proposed strengthening is applicable during thermal cycling and mechanical loading around 1273 K and up to 30% strain.
The optimal carbon concentration and TiC precipitate distribution for balancing strength, ductility, and thermal conductivity have not been established.
